title: Placeholder label option checks if option's parent is a select.
body: ### What is the issue with the HTML Standard? The definition of [placeholder label option](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#placeholder-label-option) still requires the `option`'s **parent node** to be the `select`: > If a `select` element has a `required` attribute specified, and has a display size of 1; and if the value of the first `option` element in the `select` element's [list of options](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-select-option-list) (if any) is the empty string, and **that `option` element's parent node is the `select` element (and not an `optgroup` element)**, then that `option` is the `select` element's placeholder label option. This seems like an oversight in the new custom-select work; as the result is a `select` is `:valid` per spec even though nothing meaningful is selected: ```html ``` Blink is not affected. [HTMLSelectElement::HasPlaceholderLabelOption](https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:third_party/blink/renderer/core/html/forms/html_select_element.cc;l=144) only looks at list item 0, and checks nothing about its parent: ```cpp auto* option_element = DynamicTo(GetListItems()[0].Get()); if (!option_element) return false; return option_element->value().empty(); ``` and [RecalcListItems](https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:third_party/blink/renderer/core/html/forms/html_select_element.cc;l=708-775) builds those list items by descendant traversal, so the wrapped option above is item `0` and the example is `:invalid` in Chrome. We probably still want the `` check, which is reachable because the list of options contains no optgroups: ```html ``` Blink (perhaps coincidentally) works for this case: [`RecalcListItems` pushes a non-nested optgroup into the list items before its own option children](https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:third_party/blink/renderer/core/html/forms/html_select_element.cc;l=742)), so item `0` is the ``, the `DynamicTo` cast fails, and there is no placeholder label option. Also /cc @josepharhar @annevk
